Across industries, the work has always started with understanding the market.

My experience spans recruitment, hospitality, business development and, most recently, environmental technology — but a consistent thread runs through all of it. Each role has meant understanding stakeholders first, then identifying real opportunities, building relationships around them, and structuring the work needed to support growth. At Oizom, that pattern took shape as large-scale government opportunity mapping; earlier, it showed up in hospitality revenue growth and international recruitment pipelines. The MBA at FLAME is where I'm formalising that instinct into a marketing and market research discipline.

About

The person behind the work.

My Story

I grew up close to Mount Abu, and started my professional life the way many business careers in India begin \u2014 with a BBA, followed by recruitment work. Two early roles, first as a US recruiter and then in international talent search, taught me how to read what a client actually needs versus what a job description says.

From there, I moved into business development in hospitality, running operations and growth for a hotel in Mount Abu. It was a different industry, but the underlying discipline — understanding a customer, building a relationship, structuring a plan — carried over directly.

That pattern is what pulled me toward an MBA in Marketing at FLAME University. Since starting, I've had the chance to study in Seoul through a Global Immersion Programme at SKK GSB, and to apply research and strategy skills directly at Oizom Instruments, where I now work on government market intelligence and B2G business development.

What Drives My Work

Curiosity about markets

Every industry I've worked in has looked different on the surface — recruitment, hospitality, environmental technology — but each one rewarded the same habit: asking why a market moves the way it does before deciding how to act on it.

Understanding stakeholders

Whether it was a hiring manager, a hotel guest, or a government department, the work only moved forward once I understood what the other side actually needed, not just what they said they wanted.

Turning research into action

Research on its own doesn't create growth. The part I care about is the translation — turning verified data and stakeholder insight into a plan a business team can actually use.

B2G Market Intelligence / Market Research

State-wise Government Opportunity Mapping

Building a B2G research and sales-enablement system across 36 states and UTs

Organisation

Oizom Instruments Pvt. Ltd.

Timeline

May 2026 – July 2026

My Role

Government Solutions Research, Strategy & Presentation Intern

Status

Ongoing

OverviewContextThe ProblemResearchApproachExecutionReflectionFrameworkResults & Impact

Overview

Oizom sells environmental monitoring technology into government departments, but had no structured, research-backed view of where the strongest opportunities sat across India's states and Union Territories. This project built that view: a research system, a qualification framework, and a library of state-specific sales presentations.

Context

The work sat within Oizom's broader B2G sales enablement effort, reporting to the VP of Sales, and covering all 28 Indian states and 8 Union Territories.

The Problem

Government sales cycles are long, and departments, budgets and priorities vary enormously by state. Without verified research on department budgets, active projects and decision-makers, the sales team had no reliable way to prioritise where to spend limited outreach effort.

Research

Research was drawn from government portals, annual budgets, department policies and Smart City initiative documentation, cross-checked against official sources for accuracy.

Approach

Each state was researched individually — departments, key officials, ongoing and upcoming projects — and mapped against Oizom's environmental monitoring product portfolio to identify concrete, solution-oriented opportunities rather than generic pitches.

Execution

Delivered as 36 state and UT-specific presentations, each built from verified departmental and budget data and structured to support the sales team's outreach conversations.

Reflection

The work sharpened how I think about qualifying opportunity at scale — prioritising by budget growth, project pipeline and product fit rather than by size or alphabetical convenience — and about translating dense government data into material a sales team can act on.

Framework

PPVVC — Government Opportunity Assessment Framework

PPain
PPower
VVision
VValue
CControl

Designed during this internship to evaluate, prioritise and qualify high-potential government sales opportunities in a consistent, repeatable way for the business development team.
